To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased water turbidity combined with low light intensities did not significantly reduce the foraging efficiency in perch.
increased turbidity and decreasing light intensity do not affect the foraging efficiency by juvenile perch.
the effects of increased water turbidity combined with reduced light intensity on the foraging efficiency by juvenile perch were not significant in 3 h feeding trials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of juvenile perch to compensate for reduced visual ability due to turbidity and low light intensity.
the effects of turbidity, which is an important factor in the shallow coastal waters of the Baltic Sea, on foraging efficiency of visually feeding fish, such juvenile perch.
the effects of turbidity on the feeding behaviour of juvenile perch.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
turbidity alone does not reduce the foraging efficiency and prey consumption of juvenile perch.
juvenile perch can cope with the turbidity and light intensities in the nursery areas of the Baltic coastal areas.
turbidity has no negative effect on the feeding of perch, although the effect of turbidity and low light intensities on the feeding of juvenile perch is not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perch are able to compensate for reduced visual ability caused by increased turbidity and reduced light intensity, but the ability to compensate is lower at the younger age.
juvenile perch are not affected by turbidity and decreased illumination in the short-term (3 h) and that the effects on foraging efficiency of perch in the field are not as severe as expected.

juvenile perch can compensate for decreased light intensity and increased turbidity, which may be a reason why the perch population is not negatively affected in the shallow coastal waters of the Baltic Sea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the foraging efficiency and growth rate of juvenile perch is not impaired by turbidity and low light intensity, which are common in the shallow coastal waters of the Baltic Sea.
perch are able to compensate for the effects of increased water turbidity and low light intensity on prey detection.
the effects of increased turbidity on the foraging efficiency and survival of juvenile perch in the shallow coastal nursery areas of the Baltic are not as dramatic as previously assumed.
